title: Sharp Non-Asymptotic Sphere-Packing Bounds for (1,1)-Criss-Cross Deletion Codes via Deleted-Slice Run-Tiering and Exact Indel-Pair Deduplication
abstract: Advancing Li, Sun, and Ge (arXiv:2611.34447v1), we prove four original combinatorial theorems sharpening non-asymptotic sphere-packing bounds for q-ary (1,1)-criss-cross deletion-correcting codes: (1) an Exact Levenshtein Diagonal-and-Swap Deduplicated Indel-Pair Bound P_indel(q,L) <= q^(L-1)(L^2(q-1)^2 + 2q - 1) achieving equality at L=2 and beating Li-Sun-Ge Lemma 6 by up to 4x in binary; (2) a Three-Tier Deleted-Slice Run-Decomposed Sphere-Packing Theorem proving via all three cases of Li-Sun-Ge's bad-subarray characterization that every X in C_2b has a deleted-column slice with rho_row(X^(-j)) <= s+1 or deleted-row slice with rho_col(X^(-i)) <= s+1, slashing eps_{2,n} by 53.3x at n=18 and 90.2x at n=27 and lowering the strict threshold for r_C > 2n + 2 log_q n - 2 from n >= 27 to n >= 18 (q=2), 15 -> 11 (q=3), 11 -> 9 (q=4), and 9 -> 8 (q=5); (3) a Rectangular m x n Sphere-Packing Converse and Exact Parity-Completion Bijection; and (4) Exact Small-Array Binary Optimal Capacities |C*(2,2,2)| = |C*(2,2,3)| = 2. Backed by 20 constructive Lean 4.36.0 theorems (0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice), zero-float exact-Q verifier, 16 SHA-256 certificates, and 66 tests.
